# Napwake

> Pauses idle Kubernetes workloads in staging, preview and dev, and wakes them on the first request.

Napwake pauses idle Kubernetes workloads in staging, preview and dev, and wakes them on the first request. It never deletes a workload or its data. It's open source (Apache 2.0): an operator, a `kubectl napwake` plugin, a Helm chart, and these docs.

It's for platform and infrastructure engineers who run non-production environments on their own Kubernetes clusters. Behind a VPN, SSO or an IP allowlist, a paused environment wakes on its first request. On the public internet, robots would wake it every few minutes, so set it to ask first. A browser then gets a Wake it button, and crawlers, scanners and API calls wake nothing. Tooling wakes it with an annotation, and the forecast learns when people come.

In short: label a Deployment, StatefulSet or namespace `napwake.dev/managed: "true"`. Napwake pauses the workload, scaling it to zero, once nothing has been active for `idleAfter` (an hour by default): CPU above its threshold, a deploy, an activity annotation or a Prometheus query all count as activity. While it's paused, its Services are routed to the doorman, a proxy that holds the first request and wakes it. With `autoResume`, a forecast wakes it 15 minutes before an hour it expects to be busy. `kubectl napwake scan` shows what's idle with nothing installed in the cluster.

Key pages, each as Markdown:

- [Installation](https://docs.napwake.dev/next/getting-started/installation.md): Helm or the Kustomize manifests, with Argo CD or Flux
- [Quickstart](https://docs.napwake.dev/next/getting-started/quickstart.md): one workload from idle to paused while idle and woken when used, measured first
- [kubectl plugin](https://docs.napwake.dev/next/getting-started/kubectl-plugin.md): scan, forecast, status, nodes, pause, wake, deps and enable
- [Opting in](https://docs.napwake.dev/next/guides/opt-in.md): the label, every setting as an annotation, namespaces, Kustomize and GitOps
- [Public preview environments](https://docs.napwake.dev/next/guides/preview-environments.md): asking before waking, so on a public URL a click on the page wakes it, and crawlers, scanners and API calls wake nothing
- [Idle detection](https://docs.napwake.dev/next/concepts/idle-detection.md): what counts as activity, and when a workload pauses
- [Wake on request](https://docs.napwake.dev/next/concepts/wake-on-request.md): how the doorman holds a request and wakes a paused workload
- [Forecasting](https://docs.napwake.dev/next/concepts/forecasting.md): the Holt-Winters model, `autoResume` and `pauseEarly`
- [GitOps tools](https://docs.napwake.dev/next/guides/gitops.md): leaving replicas to Napwake under Argo CD, Flux, Fleet, kapp and Kluctl
- [Labels and annotations](https://docs.napwake.dev/next/reference/labels-annotations.md): every label and annotation Napwake reads or writes
- [kubectl plugin reference](https://docs.napwake.dev/next/reference/cli.md): every flag, JSON field, exit status and permission of the plugin's commands
- [Conditions and events](https://docs.napwake.dev/next/reference/conditions-and-events.md): every status condition, with its reasons, and every event
- [Helm values](https://docs.napwake.dev/next/reference/helm-values.md): every value of the chart
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.napwake.dev/next/operations/troubleshooting.md): common problems, and how to fix them

Every page is also at its address with `.md` added. These docs name a workload's states paused, resuming and running; pictures and the home page call them asleep, waking up and awake.
